review_notes: I reviewed the whole file as supplied. I did not read any other sources or check how the definitions are used elsewhere. The four `coyonedaObjIsoForget` definitions (Mon, CommMon, AddMon, AddCommMon) share the same three-line body: `NatIso.ofComponents fun M ↦ (ConcreteCategory.homEquiv.trans (u…Hom M.carrier).symm).toIso`. The two instance blocks and the two `uliftMultiplesHom`/`uliftPowersHom` definitions are also parallel. Most of this is the usual multiplicative/additive duplication, which the `to_additive` attribute would normally cover. Here it was written by hand, probably because `ULift (Multiplicative ℕ)` and `ULift ℕ` are different types. I do not count that as a defect. The repeated body is a short composition of existing API, not nontrivial reasoning. A shared helper would need a generic concrete-category setup with the right universe and carrier hypotheses. It would be a thin wrapper that adds more machinery than it removes, and I could not show a rewrite that compiles or improves on the current code. The rubric rules out short calculations and thin wrappers, so I report no finding. The remaining uncertainty is whether a `to_additive`-based refactor would work here, which I could not check without running Lean.
